work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = m*(64+0.256+3.8355) + m*(64+0.256+1.872) + <= 2^21.9 with m = isqrt(floor(2N/5)) + 1, N = (r-1)/2^20; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. Score = log2(W(2^20)).
heuristics: None for the success probability: k1 is uniform over [0,N) (the d-th power map is exactly d-to-1 onto the order-N subgroup); block j covers exactly the m values {(m1*j + i) mod N : i < m} with consecutive arcs disjoint (start spacing m1 > m, no start collisions for window spans), so every offset covers at least (m-1)m values - an exact per-offset bound of 0.4 - 2^-118 >= 0.39 including all wrap-around hits; the closed form is additionally crosschecked against an exhaustive every-offset brute force on five smaller parameter sets.

All table machinery is deterministic with worst-case upper bounds enforced by assertion in the experiment, and every instruction allowance carries a complete line-item breakdown: merge sort over an auxiliary buffer (<= m*117 key compares at 15 instructions: six limb loads + compares + branch; <= m*118 record moves at 50 instructions including the final copy-back; <= 16 instructions key preparation per record), binary search (exactly floor(log2 m)+1 = 117 probes worst case - candidate range at most halves per probe - each <= 32 instructions: 2-word midpoint 6, pointer + record loads 4, six-limb key load/compare 12, parity bit 2, interval update + termination + branches 8), layer-batched BLOCKED fixed-base comb (2^24 scalars per block; 32 window additions per 255-bit scalar, each exactly one reference batched-incomplete-affine operation by the cost model's definition, every window layer's additions within a block sharing ONE Montgomery batched inversion; block working storage <= 256 bytes per record <= 2^32 bytes total; <= 304 instructions of addressing and control per multiplication; charged 64 units = 2x the construction) - the toy EXECUTES this blocked construction for its baby and giant point sets (5 blocks of 64, per-block pending and accumulator sizes recorded and bounded), with equality to plain double-and-add asserted in full on the baby side and on every giant point of trial 0 plus 8 random giants per trial, with addition/inversion counts reported, 512-instruction mod-r multiplication (explicit 5x52 schoolbook + Montgomery), and the runtime factorization of r-1 as a deterministic, hard-capped, counted Brent-Pollard rho construction on the fixed public input (cap checked BEFORE each consumed batch: a completed cycle provably uses at most 2^17 iterations; hard 12-cycle guard; per-iteration charge 1056 instructions = two 512-instruction modular multiplications plus 32 of loop work; joint worst case with the backtrack scan inside the shared per-cycle cap: 12 x 2^17 iterations x at most 1536 instructions per iteration = 2,415,919,104 = 2^31.169925 instructions = 2^20.204141 units, plus certification and comb tables <= 2^20.3 units total, inside the 2^21 preprocessing budget (every figure computed, not hand-rounded); Part A executes it on the production r-1, measuring 111,717 modular multiplications, 310 gcds and 9 cycles, and asserts the result equals the supplied factor list in both directions; a cap abort fails the run and demonstrably does not fire; no probabilistic model is used anywhere). The sort key is (x, y mod 2), which uniquely determines an affine point on this odd-prime curve (same-x points have opposite y-parities), so every key match is an exact point match and k1 = (i + m1*j) mod N is exact with no sign ambiguity.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold; deterministic full coverage costs about +0.86 log2.
The bound applies only for n >= 2^20; smaller n would force a smaller divisor of r-1.

Peak memory by phase: the global peak is the sort phase (main sorted array plus merge buffer = 256*m = 2^124.767581 bytes); during blocked giant generation only the sorted baby table (128m) plus O(2^32 bytes) of block scratch is live. Strictly above 2^124.7675 bytes, reported rounded up as 124.8.
Cheon's auxiliary-input attack is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel algorithm; first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
